finding: The table that decides the default, and that is the only place an operator is told what the field buys, states its savings under two preconditions it never names, and this release's own new text makes one of them unreachable for the operator it addresses. (1) Set time. §2 decided this round that `clean` is stamped at record time, not recomputed live, and `consecutive_clean` is a trailing run over the stored flags (engine/reviewstate.go:429-438 walks backwards and breaks on the first `!rounds[i].Clean`). So a round recorded before the knob is set keeps `clean: false` forever, and setting `blocking` at round k converges no earlier than k + audit_clean_rounds however advisory rounds 1..k were. §2.1's cells -- `blocking` at round 3 against `all` at round 9 -- are only reachable when the field is set before round 1 is recorded. §2.1 instead closes with `an operator who sets it accepts that trade with the numbers in front of them`, and the numbers that would justify the trade for a given cycle are that cycle's audit rounds, which do not exist yet at the only moment the table's savings are available. §3 hardens this: mid-phase setting is now the expensive path (a fenced write halts the run and spends an operator turn), so the realistic set times are exactly the two the table does not price. (2) `audit_clean_rounds`. Test 10 states that the replay is asserted `at audit_clean_rounds: 2, stated because at 1 the first pair is 2 and 8` -- so the table's four numbers move with a second workflow field. §7 knows both conditions; §2.1, the section a default decision and its documentation are derived from, states neither, and a reader choosing the knob reads §2.1, not the test list.
suggestion: Add both preconditions to §2.1 in one sentence each, next to the table rather than in §7: that the cells assume the field resolved to its value before the cycle's first round was recorded, because §2's record-time stamping means a later set cannot re-grade stored rounds, so a set at round k converges no earlier than k + audit_clean_rounds; and that the cells are computed at audit_clean_rounds: 2. Then say plainly which set time the release supports -- if it is `before the phase opens`, §2.1's closing sentence about numbers in front of the operator should point at the previous cycle's corpus (which exists) rather than this one's (which does not), and the fence's refusal message in §3 should say the same, since it is the one place a unit's operator meets the decision.

finding: The fence is twice as wide as the argument that justifies it, and the extra half costs the most expensive round-trip tp has. §3 opens by naming the risk exactly -- `the first string-valued workflow field whose non-default value relaxes a gate` -- and then fences both values on this ground: `The fence is on the field, not the direction: a unit that can set `all` can set `blocking` on the next line, so a direction-scoped fence is one a unit walks around.` That argument refutes a fence scoped to the transition (refuse a write that weakens the current value), which a unit can indeed walk around by writing from a state with no stored prior. It does not reach a fence scoped to the literal: refusing any write of `blocking`, from any state, by any path, has no walk-around, because every route to `blocking` is a write of `blocking`. So fencing `all` -- the built-in default, the value the release recommends, and the only value that can tighten the gate rather than relax it -- buys nothing the narrower fence does not already buy. Its price is not a refused command: under `tp run` a fenced write exits 2, the unit records an escalation, the run stops with `stop_reason: escalation`, and a human turn plus a fresh `tp run` is spent -- for a write that cannot end a phase early. §3 routes `tp import` into the same fence, so the halt is reachable from routine decomposition: a task file carrying `audit_converge_on: all` as an explicit override is un-importable under a run, with no lint or validate signal ahead of the import to warn the decomposer. Test 11 pins the cost rather than the value: it asserts exit 2 `for both `all` and `blocking``, doubling the assertions on all three paths.
suggestion: Scope the fence to the value that relaxes the gate: every write path refuses `blocking` under TP_UNATTENDED=1 and lets `all` through, and replace the direction argument with the reason it actually supports -- a value-scoped fence has no walk-around because every route to `blocking` writes `blocking`. Halve test 11 accordingly and add one assertion that a unit may write `all` under TP_UNATTENDED=1 (the killing mutation is a fence keyed on the field name). If refusing `all` is deliberate -- for instance because no unit may touch convergence policy at all, in either direction -- state that as the rationale and price it: name that an import of a task file carrying `audit_converge_on: all` halts a run, and say what warns the decomposer before the import unit runs.

finding: §4 cites `nonblocking_open` as the precedent -- `It is emitted unconditionally and survives --compact, on the same grounds the review side gives for nonblocking_open` -- and takes half of it. The twin is conditional, and the shipped comment says so in the same breath as the --compact grounds this release is borrowing: review_status.go:130-134, `Emitted solely when that round is clean and the count is positive, so the field's mere presence signals the accepted-open state; absent on a non-clean latest round, on a clean one with zero non-blocking survivors, and under review_converge_on=all` (review_record.go:224-231 is the same). The conditionality is not incidental to the --compact argument, it is what makes it true: the field survives --compact because its presence is itself the decision, and a key emitted on every payload signals nothing by being there. Dropping that half has three costs. (a) The signal is gone: an agent must read the map's contents to learn what the presence of the key would have told it. (b) It lands on every `tp audit --merge` of every project, and the default is `all` (§2), which is the one case the twin excludes by name -- under `all` any non-PASS row blocks, so the breakdown changes no convergence decision there, and it is derivable from the merged rows that same command emits. (c) §1 then advertises that as the benefit: `Emitted unconditionally, so it is the one part every project sees` -- the sentence sells the cost half of the trade as the value.
suggestion: Keep --compact survival (the grounds hold) and restore the conditionality the precedent supplies: emit `by_severity` only when the round has at least one non-`PASS` row, so absence means nothing was graded away and presence beside `clean: true` is the discounted-round signal, exactly as `nonblocking_open` behaves. Reword §1's third deliverable from `Emitted unconditionally, so it is the one part every project sees` to what it then is -- the breakdown a project sees when a round had non-`PASS` rows. Test 13 already asserts presence over a mixed round and survival under --compact; add the arm the change needs, a clean-under-`all` round with no non-`PASS` rows where the key is absent (the killing mutation is unconditional emission of an empty map).

finding: Three findings formed and dropped after checking them against the tree or against my own earlier rounds, recorded per this round instruction. (1) I was about to file §3's `This release adds audit-converge-on to that enum` as unbounded enum growth -- one --decision value per fenced field forever -- and propose a generic value carrying the field name. Killed: escalate.go:41 lists the shipped set as skip-gate, raise-review-cap, raise-audit-cap, import-force, other, and two of those four are already per-field names. §3 follows the established convention rather than setting a precedent, and the generic form would put the field name back in free text, which is the cost §3 correctly names. (2) I was about to file §4's `A row with an unrecognised severity is counted under the literal it carries, and one with none under null` as an unbounded, agent-controlled key space that no consumer can write a fixed parse against, given that §2 says severity is self-declared and nothing validates it. Killed by measurement: audit_merge.go:61-76 already keys `by_status` on the raw status string and `by_role` on the raw role string, and §6.6 keeps `AuditRowIsPass` byte-exact on `PASS`, so every status other than PASS is already an open key on this same summary. `by_severity` introduces no new class of key, and bucketing the literals would hide exactly the row §4 says the breakdown must not hide. (3) I was about to file that §4 puts the breakdown on `--merge` while the verdict it is meant to explain, `clean`, is emitted by `--record` (audit_record.go:100) and never by `--merge`, so the reader of `clean: true` holds the breakdown only if it retained the previous command's output. Killed by my own rounds 5 and 6, which argued for `--merge` on exactly the ground that the loop runs it on the same deduped rows immediately before `--record` and that the four pins in §6.4 do not reach it. The repair took that reasoning; re-litigating the placement now would re-open a closed decision and its only alternative is the surface §6.4 prices.
suggestion: No change requested. Recorded so a later round does not spend itself re-deriving these three, and so the reasons stay attached to the decisions they clear: the enum name (established convention), the open key space (already the shape of this summary), and the merge placement (chosen, with the counterpart deferred in §6.4).
